newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices hit high on strong sentiment.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices hit high on strong sentiment.

text.p: China stocks ended sharply up on Monday and the B shares indices hit new highs for the year, with investors encouraged by positive economic data released by Beijing last week, brokers said.
China expects to record gross domestic product growth (GDP) of 10 percent in 1997 with retail price inflation staying below five percent, the State Statistical Bureau said on Friday.
Shanghai's B share index hit its highest level since January 20, 1994, in intraday trading, with institutions seen targetting blue-chip stocks, brokers said.

But the index was pulled off its highs by some profit-taking from retail investors later in the afternoon, they added. It closed up 3.013 points, or 3.56 percent, to 87.530 on volume of 69.417 million shares worth $36.359 million.
"The market tone is bullish, but it is likely to take a rest around the current level before another run up towards 100 points," said one broker.
Shanghai Friendship & Overseas Chinese was the star on its 1996 dividend and bonus issue plans, surging $0.054 or 9.89 percent to $0.600 on volume of 3.0 million shares.
Shanghai Chlor Alkai was the most actively traded share on institutional buying, gaining $0.006 or 1.81 percent to $0.336 on volume of 3.9 million shares.
Shenzhen's B index closed at its highest level this year for the third straight session due to heavy buying of large capitalisation companies by investors, despite some profit-taking, analysts said.
The B index rose 0.69 points or 0.38 percent to 181.79 on turnover of HK$368.4 million.
Wafangdian was the most actively traded stock, soaring HK$0.64 or 9.98 percent to end at HK$7.05, making it the second best performer.
Conglomerate China Vanke was the biggest gainer, adding HK$0.78 to reach its 10 percent limit-up at HK$8.58.
The Shanghai A share index ended firmer on bullish sentiment, but is probably heading for a correction in the short term, brokers said.
The index rose 24.500 points or 1.75 percent to 1,424.106 on volume of 11.8 billion shares worth 13.2 billion yuan. The SSE30 index climbed 86.049 points or 2.39 percent to 3,682.336.
The Shenzhen A share index rose 9.54 points or 2.06 percent to 471.50 on turnover of 12.26 billion yuan against Friday's 8.46 billion.
